46: // ─── M11B Client ─────────────────────────────────────────────
47: 
48: /**
49:  * Client for the M11B Activity Room WebSocket.
50:  *
51:  * Handles:
52:  * - Connection lifecycle with auto-reconnect
53:  * - Subscribe/ack protocol
54:  * - Catch-up delivery
55:  * - Heartbeat response
56:  * - Resync directives
57:  * - Bounded backpressure (resync on buffer overflow)
58:  */
59: export class M11BClient {
60:   private ws: WebSocket | null = null;
61:   private state: M11BConnectionState = 'offline';
62:   private intentionalClose = false;
63:   private backoffMs = 1000;
64:   private reconnectTimer: number | null = null;
65:   private heartbeatTimer: number | null = null;
66:   private lastSequence = 0;
67: 
68:   // Listener sets
69:   private activityListeners = new Set<ActivityListener>();
70:   private stateListeners = new Set<StateListener>();
71:   private subscribedListeners = new Set<SubscribedListener>();
72:   private catchupCompleteListeners = new Set<CatchupCompleteListener>();
73:   private resyncListeners = new Set<ResyncListener>();
74:   private errorListeners = new Set<ErrorListener>();
75:   private heartbeatListeners = new Set<HeartbeatListener>();
76: 
77:   /** The afterSequence used in the last subscribe call. */
78:   get subscribedSequence(): number {
79:     return this.lastSequence;
80:   }
81: 
82:   /** Current connection state. */
83:   getState(): M11BConnectionState {
84:     return this.state;
85:   }
86: 
87:   // ─── Lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────
88: 
89:   /**
90:    * Connect and subscribe from a given sequence.
91:    * This is the primary entry point after HTTP snapshot.
92:    */
93:   connect(afterSequence: number): void {
94:     this.lastSequence = Math.max(0, afterSequence);
95:     this.intentionalClose = false;
96:     this._connect();
97:   }
98: 
99:   /**
100:    * Reconnect from the last known sequence.
101:    * Used after disconnect/reconnect lifecycle.
102:    */
103:   reconnect(): void {
104:     this.connect(this.lastSequence);
105:   }
106: 
107:   /**
108:    * Gracefully disconnect.
109:    */
110:   disconnect(): void {
111:     this.intentionalClose = true;
112:     this._clearTimers();
113:     if (this.ws) {
114:       this.ws.close();
115:       this.ws = null;
116:     }
117:     this.setState('offline');
118:   }
119: 
120:   // ─── Protocol Operations ──────────────────────────────────
121: 
122:   /** Send an ack for a received activity sequence. */
123:   ack(sequence: number): void {
124:     this.send({ op: 'ack', sequence });
125:   }
126: 
127:   /** Send a ping to verify connection liveness. */
128:   ping(): void {
129:     this.send({ op: 'ping' });
130:   }
131: 
132:   /** Send unsubscribe (before disconnect). */
133:   unsubscribe(): void {
134:     this.send({ op: 'unsubscribe' });
135:   }
136: 
137:   // ─── Listener Registration ────────────────────────────────
138: 
139:   onActivity(listener: ActivityListener): () => void {
140:     this.activityListeners.add(listener);
141:     return () => { this.activityListeners.delete(listener); };
142:   }
143: 
144:   onState(listener: StateListener): () => void {
145:     this.stateListeners.add(listener);
146:     listener(this.state); // Emit current state immediately
147:     return () => { this.stateListeners.delete(listener); };
148:   }
149: 
150:   onSubscribed(listener: SubscribedListener): () => void {
151:     this.subscribedListeners.add(listener);
152:     return () => { this.subscribedListeners.delete(listener); };
153:   }
154: 
155:   onCatchupComplete(listener: CatchupCompleteListener): () => void {
156:     this.catchupCompleteListeners.add(listener);
157:     return () => { this.catchupCompleteListeners.delete(listener); };
158:   }
159: 
160:   onResync(listener: ResyncListener): () => void {
161:     this.resyncListeners.add(listener);
162:     return () => { this.resyncListeners.delete(listener); };
163:   }
164: 
165:   onError(listener: ErrorListener): () => void {
166:     this.errorListeners.add(listener);
167:     return () => { this.errorListeners.delete(listener); };
168:   }
169: 
170:   onHeartbeat(listener: HeartbeatListener): () => void {
171:     this.heartbeatListeners.add(listener);
172:     return () => { this.heartbeatListeners.delete(listener); };
173:   }
174: 
175:   // ─── Internal ─────────────────────────────────────────────
176: 
177:   private _connect(): void {
178:     if (this.ws && (this.ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN || this.ws.readyState === WebSocket.CONNECTING)) {
179:       return;
180:     }
181: 
182:     this.setState('connecting');
183:     const url = resolveWsUrl('/ws/activity-room/v1');
184: 
185:     try {
186:       this.ws = new WebSocket(url);
187:     } catch {
188:       this.setState('offline');
189:       this.scheduleReconnect();
190:       return;
191:     }
192: 
193:     this.ws.onopen = () => {
194:       this.backoffMs = 1000;
195:       this.send({ op: 'subscribe', afterSequence: this.lastSequence });
196:       this.startHeartbeat();
197:     };
198: 
199:     this.ws.onmessage = (event) => {
200:       let parsed: unknown;
201:       try {
202:         parsed = JSON.parse(String(event.data));
203:       } catch {
204:         return; // Ignore malformed frames
205:       }
206: 
207:       if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== 'object') return;
208:       const msg = parsed as Record<string, unknown>;
209: 
210:       if (msg.op === 'subscribed') {
211:         const cursor = msg.cursor as ActivityCursor;
212:         const frontier = typeof msg.frontier === 'number' ? msg.frontier : 0;
213:         this.setState('live');
214:         for (const listener of this.subscribedListeners) listener(cursor, frontier);
215:         return;
216:       }
217: 
218:       if (msg.op === 'activity') {
219:         const activity = msg.activity as M11AActivityRecord;
220:         const sequence = typeof msg.sequence === 'number' ? msg.sequence : 0;
221:         if (sequence > this.lastSequence) this.lastSequence = sequence;
222:         for (const listener of this.activityListeners) listener(activity, sequence);
223:         return;
224:       }
225: 
226:       if (msg.op === 'catchup-complete') {
227:         const cursor = msg.cursor as ActivityCursor;
228:         for (const listener of this.catchupCompleteListeners) listener(cursor);
229:         return;
230:       }
231: 
232:       if (msg.op === 'resync-required') {
233:         const earliest = typeof msg.earliestAvailableSequence === 'number' ? msg.earliestAvailableSequence : 0;
234:         const latest = typeof msg.latestSequence === 'number' ? msg.latestSequence : 0;
235:         for (const listener of this.resyncListeners) listener(earliest, latest);
236:         return;
237:       }
238: 
239:       if (msg.op === 'heartbeat') {
240:         this.send({ op: 'ping' }); // Respond with pong
241:         for (const listener of this.heartbeatListeners) listener();
242:         return;
243:       }
244: 
245:       if (msg.op === 'error') {
246:         const code = typeof msg.code === 'string' ? msg.code : 'unknown';
247:         const message = typeof msg.message === 'string' ? msg.message : 'Unknown error';
248:         for (const listener of this.errorListeners) listener(code, message);
249:         return;
250:       }
251: 
252:       if (msg.op === 'unsubscribed') {
253:         // Server confirmed unsubscribe
254:         return;
255:       }
256:     };
257: 
258:     this.ws.onerror = () => {
259:       // Error will be followed by close
260:     };
261: 
262:     this.ws.onclose = () => {
263:       this.ws = null;
264:       this.stopHeartbeat();
265:       if (this.intentionalClose) {
266:         this.setState('offline');
267:       } else {
268:         this.setState('reconnecting');
269:         this.scheduleReconnect();
270:       }
271:     };
272:   }
273: 
274:   private send(message: M11BClientMessage): void {
275:     if (this.ws && this.ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) {
276:       try {
277:         this.ws.send(JSON.stringify(message));
278:       } catch {
279:         // Serialization failure — will trigger close/error
280:       }
281:     }
282:   }
283: 
284:   private setState(state: M11BConnectionState): void {
285:     if (this.state === state) return;
286:     this.state = state;
287:     for (const listener of this.stateListeners) listener(state);
288:   }
289: 
290:   private scheduleReconnect(): void {
291:     if (this.reconnectTimer !== null) return;
292:     this.reconnectTimer = window.setTimeout(() => {
293:       this.reconnectTimer = null;
294:       this._connect();
295:     }, this.backoffMs);
296:     this.backoffMs = Math.min(30_000, this.backoffMs * 2);
297:   }
298: 
299:   private startHeartbeat(): void {
300:     this.stopHeartbeat();
301:     this.heartbeatTimer = window.setInterval(() => {
302:       this.ping();
303:     }, 30_000);
304:   }
305: 
306:   private stopHeartbeat(): void {
307:     if (this.heartbeatTimer !== null) {
308:       window.clearInterval(this.heartbeatTimer);
309:       this.heartbeatTimer = null;
310:     }
311:   }
312: 
313:   private _clearTimers(): void {
314:     if (this.reconnectTimer !== null) {
315:       window.clearTimeout(this.reconnectTimer);
316:       this.reconnectTimer = null;
317:     }
318:     this.stopHeartbeat();
319:   }
320: }

1: /**
2:  * ARX-015: Agent Lifecycle Bridge
3:  *
4:  * Subscribes to harness/runtime lifecycle events (`harness.*`) and re-emits
5:  * canonical agent lifecycle events (`agent:started`, `agent:completed`) on the
6:  * EventBus. This is the integration boundary between harness-internal event
7:  * namespaces and the canonical Activity Room agent lifecycle contract.
8:  *
9:  * The bridge resolves model/provider metadata from AgentStorage so the M9
10:  * durable record carries enough identity for M10 to project agent participants
11:  * with their assigned model name.
12:  *
13:  * Design constraints:
14:  *   - Does NOT modify the harness event contract
15:  *   - Does NOT create a second participant authority
16:  *   - Preserves stable agent identity (agentId) independently from model display
17:  *   - Follows the OrchestrationEventBridge composition-root pattern
18:  */
19: 
20: import type { EventBus } from '@vestara/event-bus';
21: import type { VestaraEvent } from '@vestara/shared';
22: 
23: /** Minimal interface for resolving agent model configuration. */
24: export interface AgentModelResolver {
25:   resolve(input: { agentId: string }): Promise<
26:     | {
27:         providerId?: string;
28:         modelId?: string;
29:         role?: string;
30:         displayName?: string;
31:         modelDisplayName?: string;
32:       }
33:     | undefined
34:   >;
35: }
36: 
37: export interface AgentLifecycleBridgeOptions {
38:   readonly eventBus: EventBus;
39:   readonly agentModelResolver: AgentModelResolver;
40: }
41: 
42: /** Identity fields carried in harness.* event payloads. */
43: interface HarnessIdentity {
44:   readonly agentId?: unknown;
45:   readonly threadId?: unknown;
46:   readonly turnId?: unknown;
47:   readonly runId?: unknown;
48:   readonly correlationId?: unknown;
49:   readonly causationId?: unknown;
50: }
51: 
52: /**
53:  * Create the Agent lifecycle bridge. Returns an unsubscribe function.
54:  *
55:  * The bridge subscribes to `harness.*` events and:
56:  *   1. Filters to turn lifecycle events (started/completed/cancelled)
57:  *   2. Resolves the agent's model configuration
58:  *   3. Emits canonical `agent:started`/`agent:completed` events
59:  *
60:  * The M9IngestionBridge then ingests these canonical events normally.
61:  */
62: export function createAgentLifecycleBridge(options: AgentLifecycleBridgeOptions): () => void {
63:   const handler = async (event: VestaraEvent): Promise<void> => {
64:     try {
65:       const payload = event.payload as HarnessIdentity & Record<string, unknown>;
66:       const agentId = typeof payload.agentId === 'string' && payload.agentId ? payload.agentId : '';
67:       if (!agentId) return;
68: 
69:       // Map harness event types to canonical agent lifecycle types
70:       const lifecycleType = mapHarnessToLifecycle(event.type);
71:       if (!lifecycleType) return;
72: 
73:       // Resolve model metadata from agent configuration
74:       const resolved = await options.agentModelResolver.resolve({ agentId });
75: 
76:       // displayName = canonical identity (agentId for unnamed agents)
77:       // modelDisplayName = presentation-only model name (for unnamed AI fallback)
78:       const modelDisplayName = resolved?.modelDisplayName || resolved?.displayName;
79: 
80:       // Emit canonical agent lifecycle event for M9 bridge ingestion
81:       await options.eventBus
82:         .emit({
83:           type: `agent:${lifecycleType}`,
84:           source: 'agent-lifecycle-bridge',
85:           actor: { id: agentId, role: 'agent' },
86:           payload: {
87:             agentId,
88:             displayName: agentId,
89:             modelDisplayName,
90:             role: resolved?.role || agentId,
91:             modelId: resolved?.modelId,
92:             providerId: resolved?.providerId,
93:             task: (payload as Record<string, unknown>).instruction ?? (payload as Record<string, unknown>).task,
94:           },
95:           metadata: {
96:             correlationId:
97:               typeof payload.correlationId === 'string' ? payload.correlationId : event.metadata?.correlationId,
98:             causationId: typeof payload.causationId === 'string' ? payload.causationId : event.metadata?.causationId,
99:             executionId: event.metadata?.executionId,
100:             traceId: event.metadata?.traceId,
101:           },
102:         })
103:         .catch(() => {
104:           /* bridge failures must never break the harness run */
105:         });
106:     } catch {
107:       /* best-effort — swallow all errors */
108:     }
109:   };
110: 
111:   return options.eventBus.subscribe('harness.*', handler);
112: }
113: 
114: /**
115:  * Map harness event types to canonical agent lifecycle types.
116:  * Returns undefined for events that don't represent agent lifecycle transitions.
117:  */
118: function mapHarnessToLifecycle(type: string): 'started' | 'completed' | 'failed' | 'cancelled' | 'progress' | null {
119:   if (type === 'harness.turn.started') return 'started';
120:   if (type === 'harness.outcome.completed') return 'completed';
121:   if (type === 'harness.outcome.failed') return 'failed';
122:   if (type === 'harness.outcome.cancelled') return 'cancelled';
123:   if (type === 'harness.model.started') return 'progress';
124:   return null;

state.title: node -e "const fs=require('fs');require('sql.js')().then(SQL=>{const db=new SQL.Database(fs.readFileSync('.vestara/activity.db'));const q=\"SELECT sequence,id,kind,payload_json FROM activity_events ORDER BY sequence\";const rows=db.exec(q)[0]?.values||[]; const out=rows.map(r=>{let p={};try{p=JSON.parse(r[3])}catch{};return [r[0],r[1],r[2],p.actor,p.agentId,p.workflowId,p.sessionId,p.messageKind,String(p.content||'').slice(0,120)]}).filter(r=>JSON.stringify(r).match(/local|assistant|workspace-ui|sim-principal|mimo-test|ux-test|state-test/i));console.log(JSON.stringify(out,null,2));db.close()})"

1: /**
2:  * @vestara/conversation — Conversation Service
3:  *
4:  * Orchestrates the conversation lifecycle: create, sendMessage,
5:  * receiveResponse, closeConversation, listConversations. Wires
6:  * through the Context Assembler and AI Provider. Emits events
7:  * at every stage.
8:  *
9:  * Architecture Traceability:
10:  *   Foundation: VESTARA-OBJECT-MODEL.md → VOM-Conversation, VOM-Message
11:  *   Specification: CAP-001 → Workspace.Chat
12:  *   Runtime: LIFECYCLE-SPECIFICATION.md → Conversation Lifecycle
13:  */
14: 
15: import type { ContextAssembler } from '@vestara/context';
16: import type { EventBus } from '@vestara/event-bus';
17: import type { Logger } from '@vestara/logger';
18: import type {
19:   CompletionRequest,
20:   CompletionResponse,
21:   Conversation,
22:   ConversationSummary,
23:   Message,
24:   StreamChunk,
25:   ToolObservation,
26: } from '@vestara/shared';
27: import { DefaultStreamProcessor } from '@vestara/stream';
28: 
29: export interface ProviderExecutor {
30:   complete(request: CompletionRequest): Promise<CompletionResponse>;
31:   stream(request: CompletionRequest): AsyncIterable<StreamChunk>;
32: }
33: 
34: /**
35:  * Persistence boundary for conversations. `DefaultConversationService` keeps an
36:  * in-memory map by default; pass a store (e.g. the SQLite store in
37:  * `@vestara/conversation-runtime`) to survive restart. All mutations flow
38:  * through the service as the single writer.
39:  */
40: export interface ConversationStore {
41:   create(conversation: Conversation): Promise<void>;
42:   get(id: string): Promise<Conversation | null>;
43:   getConversation(
44:     id: string,
45:     options?: { limit?: number; offset?: number; order?: 'asc' | 'desc' },
46:   ): Promise<Conversation | null>;
47:   list(userId: string): Promise<ConversationSummary[]>;
48:   /** VES-PERF-001C: bounded summary page for conversation history. */
49:   listPage(userId: string, options?: { limit?: number; offset?: number }): Promise<ConversationListPage>;
50:   addMessage(conversationId: string, message: Message): Promise<void>;
51:   setStatus(id: string, status: Conversation['status']): Promise<void>;
52:   updateTitle(id: string, title: string): Promise<void>;
53:   updateRuntimeSessionId(id: string, runtimeSessionId: string): Promise<void>;
54:   remove(id: string): Promise<void>;
55: }
56: 
57: /**
58:  * VES-PERF-001C: a bounded, metadata-only page of conversation summaries.
59:  * Never contains message bodies — history stays a lightweight projection.
60:  */
61: export interface ConversationListPage {
62:   conversations: ConversationSummary[];
63:   total: number;
64:   offset: number;
65:   limit: number;
66:   hasMore: boolean;
67: }
68: 
69: export interface ConversationService {
70:   createConversation(userId?: string, options?: { runtimeSessionId?: string }): Promise<Conversation>;
71:   sendMessage(conversationId: string, content: string, options?: SendOptions): Promise<SendResult>;
72:   closeConversation(conversationId: string): Promise<void>;
73:   listConversations(userId?: string): Promise<ConversationSummary[]>;
74:   /** VES-PERF-001C: bounded summary page (metadata only; never message bodies). */
75:   listConversationsPage(userId?: string, options?: { limit?: number; offset?: number }): Promise<ConversationListPage>;
76:   getConversation(
77:     id: string,
78:     options?: { limit?: number; offset?: number; order?: 'asc' | 'desc' },
79:   ): Promise<Conversation | null>;
80:   deleteConversation(id: string): Promise<void>;
81:   sendMessageStream(conversationId: string, content: string, options?: SendOptions): AsyncIterable<StreamChunk>;
82: }
83: 
84: export interface SendOptions {
85:   model?: string;
86:   /**
87:    * GA-RUNTIME-001: requested upstream provider ID (browser selection).
88:    * Bounded server-side; never trusted as execution authority.
89:    */
90:   provider?: string;
91:   temperature?: number;
92:   maxTokens?: number;
93:   systemPrompt?: string;
94:   /** Trusted turn-time surface context (GA-CONTEXT-002). Optional, turn-scoped. */
95:   surfaceContext?: import('@vestara/shared').TurnSurfaceContext;
96:   /** OpenCode session ID for session reuse. When set, the adapter reuses the existing session. */
97:   runtimeSessionId?: string;
98:   /** GA-RUNTIME-001: caller-controlled cancellation (client disconnect / stop). */
99:   signal?: AbortSignal;
100:   /**
101:    * GA-EXEC-001: per-turn execution configuration (turnTimeoutMs,
102:    * maxOperations, maxToolCalls). Passed through to the provider executor
103:    * so the adapter can enforce Vestara-owned limits.
104:    */
105:   executionConfig?: import('@vestara/shared').GAExecutionConfig;
106: }

108: export interface SendResult {
109:   message: Message;
110:   response: Message;
111:   latency: number;

114: let conversationCounter = 0;
115: let messageCounter = 0;

117: function generateId(prefix: string): string {

121: export class DefaultConversationService implements ConversationService {
122:   private conversations: Map<string, Conversation> = new Map();
123:   private contextAssembler: ContextAssembler;
124:   private providerExecutor: ProviderExecutor;
125:   private eventBus?: EventBus;
126:   private logger?: Logger;
127:   private store?: ConversationStore;
128: 
129:   constructor(options: {
130:     contextAssembler: ContextAssembler;
131:     providerExecutor: ProviderExecutor;
132:     eventBus?: EventBus;
133:     logger?: Logger;
134:     store?: ConversationStore;
135:   }) {
136:     this.contextAssembler = options.contextAssembler;
137:     this.providerExecutor = options.providerExecutor;

143:   /** Unbounded load — caches the complete conversation for internal operations. */
144:   private async loadIntoMemory(id: string): Promise<Conversation | null> {
145:     if (!this.store) return this.conversations.get(id) ?? null;
146:     const persisted = await this.store.get(id);

149:   }

166:   async createConversation(userId = 'local', options?: { runtimeSessionId?: string }): Promise<Conversation> {

178:       updatedAt: now,

180: 
181:     this.conversations.set(id, conversation);
182:     await this.store?.create(conversation);
183: 
184:     await this.eventBus?.emit({
185:       type: 'conversation:created',
186:       source: 'conversation-service',
187:       payload: { conversationId: id, userId, title: conversation.title },

193:       conversationId: id,

218:       type: 'conversation:message.sent',

220:       payload: { conversationId, messageId: userMessage.id, content },
221:       actor: { id: conversation.userId, role: 'user' },

223:     });

231:     // Build context and send to provider

238:       type: 'conversation:provider.request.started',

1: /**
2:  * Assistant OpenCode Adapter — OpenCode 1.18.27 → Vestara Assistant SSE.
3:  *
4:  * GA-UX-PREMIUM M3 (contract/infrastructure). Drives one assistant turn over
5:  * a local OpenCode headless server: creates a session, consumes the `/event`
6:  * SSE stream, and projects runtime events into `assistant.execution.v1`
7:  * details that ride the existing Conversation SSE contract
8:  * (delta/status/tool/tool_result/done/error — additive, §13).
9:  *
10:  * Invariant: the browser consumes Vestara's projection contract, never raw
11:  * OpenCode events. React must never depend on OpenCode event schemas.
12:  *
13:  * Boundaries:
14:  * - Identity: OpenCode `callID` is preserved as `operationId` (§3).
15:  * - Lifecycle: explicit running/completed/failed; never `output === "failed"` (§4).
16:  * - Sanitization: every field passes the shared allowlist normalizer (§11).
17:  * - AR-009 remains paused: this adapter is optional wiring with graceful
18:  *   fallback to the direct-provider executor; it never makes OpenCode
19:  *   mandatory.
20:  *
21:  * Execution lifecycle semantics (GA-DETACH-001):
22:  * - COMPLETED: natural `session.status idle` received — turn finished successfully.
23:  * - FAILED: runtime error or provider failure — execution did not complete.
24:  * - TIMEOUT: configured execution deadline actually expired.
25:  * - CANCELLED: explicitly authorized cancellation (user Stop, API abort).
26:  * - DETACHED: observer/client stopped watching — execution continues server-side.
27:  *   This is NOT a failure. The session remains active for later reattachment.
28:  */
29: 
30: import type { ProviderExecutor } from '@vestara/conversation';
31: import type { OpenCodeEvent, OpenCodeHttpClient } from '@vestara/opencode-runtime';
32: import { normalizePermissionAction } from '@vestara/opencode-runtime';
33: import type { CompletionRequest, CompletionResponse, GAExecutionConfig, StreamChunk } from '@vestara/shared';
34: import {
35:   type AssistantCapabilityPolicy,
36:   buildToolsMap,
37:   evaluatePermission,
38:   type PermissionEvaluation,
39: } from './assistant-capability-policy';
40: import type { AssistantConversationSessionRegistry } from './assistant-conversation-sessions';
41: import {
42:   projectDetail,
43:   projectEditStarted,
44:   projectMessagePartUpdated,
45:   projectPermissionRequested,
46:   projectPermissionResolved,
47:   projectQuestionAsked,
48:   projectQuestionResolved,
49:   projectReadObservation,
50:   projectTerminalCompleted,
51:   projectTerminalStarted,
52:   projectTodoSnapshot,
53:   projectToolCompleted,
54:   projectToolFailed,
55:   projectToolStarted,
56: } from './assistant-execution-projection';
57: import type { AssistantInteractionBroker, AssistantQuestionDecision } from './assistant-interaction-broker';
58: 
59: export interface AssistantOpenCodeExecutorOptions {
60:   client: OpenCodeHttpClient;
61:   /** Workspace identity for the OpenCode request context. */
62:   workspaceId: string;
63:   /** Repository root (absolute) — OpenCode session directory authority. */
64:   directory: string;
65:   agent: string;
66:   /** Resolved provider/model override (when known at construction time). */
67:   model?: { providerID: string; modelID: string };
68:   /**
69:    * Per-turn resolver: map the requested `CompletionRequest.model` /
70:    * `CompletionRequest.provider` → the provider/model that actually executes.
71:    * When provided, the adapter never fabricates a provider — provenance follows
72:    * the real upstream resolution. May be async (server-authoritative binding
73:    * validation happens before the turn is submitted).
74:    */
75:   resolveProviderModel?: (
76:     model?: string,
77:     provider?: string,
78:   ) =>
79:     | { providerID: string; modelID: string }
80:     | Promise<{ providerID: string; modelID: string } | undefined>
81:     | undefined;
82:   /**
83:    * GA-RUNTIME-001: conversation → OpenCode session registry. When set and the
84:    * request carries a `conversationId`, the executor reuses the conversation's
85:    * session across turns (single-flight creation on the first turn). Session
86:    * continuity is keyed by conversation identity — never by provider/model.
87:    */
88:   sessionRegistry?: AssistantConversationSessionRegistry;
89:   /**
90:    * GA-RUNTIME-001 Addendum B: interactive permission/question decisions.
91:    * When set, ASK policy decisions and OpenCode questions project to the
92:    * browser and await a real user decision instead of degrading to a status.
93:    */
94:   interactionBroker?: AssistantInteractionBroker;
95:   title?: string;
96:   /** Hard cap for a single turn (ms). Default 5 minutes. */
97:   turnTimeoutMs?: number;
98:   /**
99:    * GA-CAP-003: Vestara-owned capability boundary for the Global Assistant.
100:    * When provided, permission requests are evaluated against this policy
101:    * before being surfaced to the user. ALLOW decisions are auto-approved,
102:    * DENY decisions are auto-rejected, and ASK decisions are surfaced.
103:    * When absent, the adapter behaves as before (all permissions surfaced).
104:    */
105:   capabilityPolicy?: AssistantCapabilityPolicy;
106: }
107: 
108: // GA-EXEC-001: Default turn timeout. Overridden by:
109: //   1. Per-turn executionConfig.turnTimeoutMs (UI/session)
110: //   2. VESTARA_GA_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS env var (deployment default)
111: const TURN_TIMEOUT_MS = Number(process.env.VESTARA_GA_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS) || 15 * 60 * 1000;
112: 
113: // GA-EXEC-001: Default per-turn tool-call budget for the Global Assistant.
114: // Bounds turns that arrive without an explicit executionConfig.maxToolCalls
115: // (e.g. Activity Room fire-and-forget turns). Explicit 0 still means
116: // unlimited; explicit 1–200 overrides this default.
117: // Fix 3 (2026-09-13): raised 30→80 so dirty-worktree/analysis turns (~60 calls) no longer hit the bound
118: // before the user touches ExecutionControls; env VESTARA_GA_MAX_TOOL_CALLS still overrides.
119: const DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS = Number(process.env.VESTARA_GA_MAX_TOOL_CALLS) || 80;
120: 
121: /**
122:  * Transport label used ONLY when no real provider resolution is available
123:  * (no resolver wired, no model override). Never replaces real upstream
124:  * provenance — callers that wire a resolver always get the true provider.
125:  */
126: const TRANSPORT_PROVIDER = 'opencode';
127: 
128: /**
129:  * GA-DETACH-001: How a turn ended. This determines whether the OpenCode
130:  * session should be aborted or left running for later reattachment.
131:  *
132:  * - COMPLETED: natural `session.status idle` — turn finished successfully.
133:  * - FAILED: runtime error — execution did not complete.
134:  * - TIMEOUT: configured deadline expired.
135:  * - CANCELLED: explicitly authorized cancellation (user Stop, API abort).
136:  * - DETACHED: observer/client stopped watching — execution continues.
137:  */
138: type TurnTermination = 'completed' | 'failed' | 'timeout' | 'cancelled' | 'detached';
139: 
140: /**
141:  * GA-DETACH-001: Whether a turn termination requires aborting the OpenCode
142:  * session. COMPLETED and DETACHED do NOT require abort — the session is
143:  * either idle or still running. CANCELLED, TIMEOUT, and FAILED require abort
144:  * to settle the session for reuse.
145:  */
146: function requiresAbort(termination: TurnTermination): boolean {
147:   return termination === 'cancelled' || termination === 'timeout' || termination === 'failed';
148: }
149: 
150: function lastUserText(messages: CompletionRequest['messages']): string {
151:   for (let i = messages.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {
152:     const message = messages[i];
153:     if (message && message.role === 'user' && typeof message.content === 'string') {
154:       return message.content;
155:     }
156:   }
157:   return '';
158: }
159: 
160: /**
161:  * Derive a meaningful OpenCode session title from the first user message.
162:  * Collapses whitespace and bounds to a single short line (48 chars).
163:  * Falls back to 'Assistant conversation' when no user text is available.
164:  */
165: function deriveSessionTitle(userText: string): string {
166:   const singleLine = userText.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
167:   if (singleLine.length === 0) return 'Assistant conversation';
168:   const maxLength = 48;
169:   if (singleLine.length <= maxLength) return singleLine;
170:   return `${singleLine.slice(0, maxLength).trimEnd()}…`;
171: }
172: 
173: /**
174:  * GA-CONTEXT-002: deterministic trusted-application-context block for the
175:  * model. Bounded, descriptive — never repository/execution authority. The
176:  * surface `path`/`route`/`title` are client navigation state; the workspace
177:  * name/id are descriptive identity. Selection label is display data only.
178:  */
179: function buildSurfaceSystem(surfaceContext: CompletionRequest['surfaceContext']): string | undefined {
180:   if (!surfaceContext?.surface || !surfaceContext.workspace) return undefined;
181:   const { workspace, surface, selected } = surfaceContext;
182:   const lines = ['Current Vestara application context:', `Workspace: ${workspace.name}`];
183:   if (surface.section) lines.push(`Section: ${surface.section}`);
184:   if (surface.title) lines.push(`Page: ${surface.title}`);
185:   if (surface.routeId) lines.push(`Route: ${surface.routeId}`);
186:   if (selected) {
187:     lines.push('Selected item:', `Type: ${selected.kind}`, `ID: ${selected.id}`);
188:     if (selected.label) lines.push(`Label: ${selected.label}`);
189:   }
190:   return lines.join('\n');
191: }
192: 
193: function chunk(type: StreamChunk['type'], sequence: number, extra: Partial<StreamChunk> = {}): StreamChunk {
194:   return {
195:     id: `oc-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(16).slice(2, 8)}`,
196:     type,
197:     metadata: { sequence, timestamp: new Date().toISOString() },
198:     ...extra,
199:   };
200: }
201: 
202: /**
203:  * Run one OpenCode turn as an async generator of normalized `StreamChunk`s.
204:  * Events are consumed from the session-scoped `/event` stream; correlation is
205:  * keyed on OpenCode `callID`; every projected detail passes the sanitizer.
206:  *
207:  * GA-RUNTIME-001: when `sessionId` is provided the OpenCode session is REUSED
208:  * (conversation continuity); when absent a fresh session is created (backward-
209:  * compatible single-turn path).
210:  */
211: export async function* runAssistantOpenCodeTurn(
212:   options: AssistantOpenCodeExecutorOptions,
213:   request: CompletionRequest,
214:   sessionId?: string,
215: ): AsyncIterable<StreamChunk> {
216:   const { client, workspaceId, directory, agent, turnTimeoutMs: defaultTimeout = TURN_TIMEOUT_MS } = options;
217:   // GA-EXEC-001: per-turn execution config from UI. Overrides defaults.
218:   const execCfg: GAExecutionConfig | undefined = request.executionConfig;
219:   const turnTimeoutMs = execCfg?.turnTimeoutMs ?? defaultTimeout;
220:   // GA-EXEC-001: maxToolCalls is the canonical tool-invocation budget.
221:   // maxOperations was removed — it counted the same events as maxToolCalls.
222:   // Falls back to DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS so unconstrained turns cannot loop
223:   // for the full 15min deadline (observed: ~100 tool calls / 3min on free tier).
224:   const maxToolCalls = execCfg?.maxToolCalls ?? DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS;
225:   const context = { workspaceId, directory };
226:   const userText = lastUserText(request.messages);
227:   if (!userText) throw new Error('Assistant OpenCode turn requires a user message');
228: 
229:   // GA-EXEC-001: tool call counter for budget enforcement
230:   let toolCallCount = 0;
231: 
232:   // Resolve the real upstream provider/model for THIS turn; never fabricated.
233:   // The requested provider/model is the browser's REQUESTED binding; the
234:   // server-side resolver validates it before execution (GA-RUNTIME-001 G).
235:   const turnModel = (await options.resolveProviderModel?.(request.model, request.provider)) ?? options.model;
236:   const turnProvider = turnModel?.providerID ?? TRANSPORT_PROVIDER;
237: 
238:   // GA-RUNTIME-001: reuse the conversation's session when the caller resolved
239:   // one; otherwise create (single-turn path).
240:   let resolvedSessionId = sessionId;
241:   if (!resolvedSessionId) {
242:     const session = await client.createSession({ title: deriveSessionTitle(userText) }, context);
243:     resolvedSessionId = session.id;
244:   }
245: 
246:   const controller = new AbortController();
247:   const onAbort = () => controller.abort();
248:   request.signal?.addEventListener('abort', onAbort);
249: 
250:   // Background event reader → FIFO queue (events may arrive before sendMessage
251:   // resolves; the queue guarantees none are dropped).
252:   const queue: OpenCodeEvent[] = [];
253:   const waiters: Array<() => void> = [];
254:   let readerDone = false;
255:   const wake = () => {
256:     const pending = waiters.splice(0);
257:     for (const waiter of pending) waiter();
258:   };
259:   const push = (event: OpenCodeEvent) => {
260:     queue.push(event);
261:     wake();
262:   };
263:   const readerPromise = (async () => {
264:     try {
265:       for await (const event of client.openEventStream(context, controller.signal)) {
266:         const payload = event.payload as Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
267:         if (payload && payload.sessionID === resolvedSessionId) push(event);
268:       }
269:     } catch {
270:       // stream closed (abort/network) — the turn loop observes readerDone.
271:     } finally {
272:       readerDone = true;
273:       wake();
274:     }
275:   })();
276: 
277:   const deadline = Date.now() + turnTimeoutMs;
278:   const shellStartedAt = new Map<string, number>();
279:   let sequence = 0;
280:   // GA-DETACH-001: Track how the turn ended. This determines whether the
281:   // OpenCode session should be aborted or left running for reattachment.
282:   let termination: TurnTermination = 'failed'; // default to failed; updated on exit
283: 
284:   try {
285:     // GA-SSE-003B: submit asynchronously (POST /session/:id/prompt_async).
286:     // sendMessage() waits for full execution and is incompatible with
287:     // interactive runtime behavior; prompt_async is accepted in ~50ms and the
288:     // already-subscribed /event stream becomes the execution authority.
289:     await client.sendMessageAsync(
290:       resolvedSessionId,
291:       {
292:         parts: [{ type: 'text', text: userText }],
293:         agent,
294:         // Async input model shape: { providerId, modelId } (lowercase).
295:         // GA-RUNTIME-001 E: provider/model is Execution Binding — it rides the
296:         // prompt, never a new session.
297:         ...(turnModel ? { model: { providerId: turnModel.providerID, modelId: turnModel.modelID } } : {}),
298:         // GA-CONTEXT-002: trusted turn-time surface context via the
299:         // established `system` field (proven additive — the agent's own
300:         // governance prompt is preserved). Never concatenated into the human
301:         // message; never repository/execution authority.
302:         ...(buildSurfaceSystem(request.surfaceContext) ? { system: buildSurfaceSystem(request.surfaceContext) } : {}),
303:         // GA-RUNTIME-004 / GA-TOOL-001: per-turn tool availability from
304:         // GA-CAP-003 policy. ALLOW → true, ASK/DENY → false. This is the
305:         // pre-execution enforcement point that prevents the * allow wildcard
306:         // from auto-approving mutation tools.
307:         ...(options.capabilityPolicy ? { tools: buildToolsMap(options.capabilityPolicy) } : {}),
308:       },
309:       context,
310:     );
311: 
312:     let turnDone = false;
313:     while (!turnDone) {
314:       if (Date.now() > deadline) {
315:         termination = 'timeout';
316:         yield chunk('error', sequence++, { content: 'Execution deadline exceeded' });
317:         break;
318:       }
319:       // GA-DETACH-001: Wait for events with deadline awareness.
320:       // Without this, the inner wait blocks indefinitely when the event
321:       // stream is open but idle, preventing the deadline from firing.
322:       while (queue.length === 0 && !readerDone) {
323:         const remaining = deadline - Date.now();
324:         if (remaining <= 0) break;
325:         await Promise.race([
326:           new Promise<void>((resolve) => waiters.push(resolve)),
327:           new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, Math.min(remaining, 1000))),
328:         ]);
329:       }
330:       // Re-check deadline after waiting — the wait may have been interrupted
331:       // by the timeout rather than a new event.
332:       if (Date.now() > deadline) {
333:         termination = 'timeout';
334:         yield chunk('error', sequence++, { content: 'Execution deadline exceeded' });
335:         break;
336:       }
337:       if (queue.length === 0 && readerDone) break;
338:       const event = queue.shift();
339:       if (!event) break;
340: 
341:       const payload = (event.payload ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
342:       const callID = typeof payload.callID === 'string' ? payload.callID : undefined;
343: 
344:       // GA-EXEC-001: budget enforcement helper — checks tool-call limits
345:       // after each event. Returns an error message if exceeded, null if
346:       // within budget. maxToolCalls=0 means unlimited (UI hook default).
347:       const checkBudget = (): string | null => {
348:         if (maxToolCalls > 0 && toolCallCount >= maxToolCalls) {
349:           return `Tool call limit reached: ${maxToolCalls} tool calls`;
350:         }
351:         return null;
352:       };
353: 
354:       switch (event.type) {
355:         case 'session.next.text.delta':
356:         case 'message.part.delta': {
357:           if (typeof payload.delta === 'string' && payload.delta) {
358:             // GA-EXEC-001: text deltas are LLM inference output, not governed
359:             // operations. They do NOT consume the maxOperations budget.
360:             yield {
361:               ...chunk('text', sequence++, { content: payload.delta }),
362:               // GA-RUNTIME-001 H: the displayed execution binding is the REAL
363:               // upstream provider/model for this turn — never the composer value.
364:               metadata: {
365:                 sequence: 0,
366:                 timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
367:                 provider: turnProvider,
368:                 model: turnModel?.modelID,
369:                 runtimeSessionId: resolvedSessionId,
370:               },
371:             };
372:           }
373:           break;
374:         }
375:         case 'message.part.updated': {
376:           // LIVE path: tool calls surface as tool parts on this event.
377:           // GA-TOOL-UX-001B: read parts project structured read evidence
378:           // (server-side wrapper parse); all other tools keep the generic
379:           // projection. Unknown tools remain generic.
380:           const detail = projectReadObservation(event, directory) ?? projectMessagePartUpdated(event);
381:           if (detail && (detail.kind === 'tool' || detail.kind === 'read')) {
382:             const toolName = detail.tool ?? 'read';
383:             if (detail.state === 'running') {
384:               toolCallCount++;
385:               const budgetError = checkBudget();
386:               if (budgetError) {
387:                 yield chunk('error', sequence++, { content: budgetError });
388:                 break;
389:               }
390:               yield chunk('tool_call', sequence++, { name: toolName, detail });
391:             } else {
392:               // Read results ride the structured detail; chunk content stays
393:               // within the M2 200-char boundary for the transient surface.
394:               const resultContent =
395:                 detail.state === 'failed'
396:                   ? (detail.error ?? 'Tool failed')
397:                   : detail.kind === 'read'
398:                     ? (detail.contentPreview ?? '').slice(0, 200) || toolName
399:                     : (detail.preview ?? '');
400:               yield chunk('tool_result', sequence++, {
401:                 name: toolName,
402:                 content: resultContent,
403:                 detail,
404:               });
405:             }
406:           }
407:           break;
408:         }
409:         case 'session.next.tool.input.started':
410:         case 'session.next.tool.called': {
411:           const detail = projectToolStarted(event);
412:           if (detail && detail.kind === 'tool') {
413:             toolCallCount++;
414:             const budgetError = checkBudget();
415:             if (budgetError) {
416:               yield chunk('error', sequence++, { content: budgetError });
417:               break;
418:             }
419:             yield chunk('tool_call', sequence++, { name: detail.tool, detail });
420:           }
421:           break;
422:         }
423:         case 'session.next.tool.success': {
424:           const detail = projectToolCompleted(event);
425:           if (detail && detail.kind === 'tool') {
426:             yield chunk('tool_result', sequence++, { name: detail.tool, content: detail.preview ?? '', detail });
427:           }
428:           break;

1: /**
2:  * GA-RUNTIME-001 — Assistant Execution Binding Resolver
3:  *
4:  * Server-authoritative provider/model resolution for the Global Assistant.
5:  * The browser's ProviderModelSelector value is a REQUESTED binding, never
6:  * authority: the server validates provider existence, model existence and
7:  * provider/model compatibility against the canonical OpenCode runtime provider
8:  * discovery before any execution happens.
9:  *
10:  *   ProviderModelSelector (browser)
11:  *        ↓ requested provider/model
12:  *   server validation/resolution  ← this resolver
13:  *        ↓
14:  *   Execution Binding { providerID, modelID }
15:  *        ↓
16:  *   OpenCode turn (prompt_async model field)
17:  *
18:  * If the requested binding cannot be resolved, a deterministic
19:  * `AssistantBindingError` is thrown (never silent fallback to a previous or
20:  * default model while displaying the requested one).
21:  *
22:  * Discovery results are cached briefly (matching the runtime provider surface
23:  * the UI is offered), so validation is cheap and consistent per turn.
24:  */
25: 
26: import type { OpenCodeHttpClient } from '@vestara/opencode-runtime';
27: 
28: export interface AssistantExecutionBinding {
29:   readonly providerID: string;
30:   readonly modelID: string;
31: }
32: 
33: export type AssistantBindingErrorCode = 'provider-not-found' | 'model-not-found' | 'runtime-unavailable';
34: 
35: export class AssistantBindingError extends Error {
36:   readonly code: AssistantBindingErrorCode;
37:   readonly providerId?: string;
38:   readonly modelId?: string;
39: 
40:   constructor(code: AssistantBindingErrorCode, message: string, details?: { providerId?: string; modelId?: string }) {
41:     super(message);
42:     this.name = 'AssistantBindingError';
43:     this.code = code;
44:     this.providerId = details?.providerId;
45:     this.modelId = details?.modelId;
46:   }
47: }
48: 
49: export interface AssistantBindingRequest {
50:   readonly providerId?: string;
51:   readonly modelId?: string;
52: }
53: 
54: export interface AssistantBindingResolver {
55:   /**
56:    * Resolve a requested provider/model to an execution binding.
57:    * With no request (or an incomplete request) the configured fallback
58:    * binding is returned. Throws `AssistantBindingError` when a requested
59:    * binding cannot be resolved deterministically.
60:    */
61:   resolve(request?: AssistantBindingRequest): Promise<AssistantExecutionBinding>;
62: }
63: 
64: const DISCOVERY_CACHE_MS = 30_000;
65: 
66: /**
67:  * Build the canonical resolver over the local OpenCode runtime client.
68:  *
69:  * @param client   the shared OpenCodeHttpClient (127.0.0.1:4096).
70:  * @param fallback the agent-assistant default binding used when the caller
71:  *                 requests no provider/model (e.g. activity-room / CLI turns).
72:  */
73: export function createAssistantBindingResolver(
74:   client: OpenCodeHttpClient,
75:   fallback: AssistantExecutionBinding | undefined,
76: ): AssistantBindingResolver {
77:   let cache: { providers: ReadonlyArray<{ id: string; models?: readonly string[] }>; at: number } | undefined;
78: 
79:   async function discover(): Promise<ReadonlyArray<{ id: string; models?: readonly string[] }>> {
80:     if (cache && Date.now() - cache.at < DISCOVERY_CACHE_MS) return cache.providers;
81:     let providers: ReadonlyArray<{ id: string; models?: readonly string[] }>;
82:     try {
83:       providers = await client.listProviders();
84:     } catch (error) {
85:       throw new AssistantBindingError(
86:         'runtime-unavailable',
87:         `Cannot validate the requested provider/model — the OpenCode runtime is unavailable (${error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'unknown'})`,
88:       );
89:     }
90:     cache = { providers, at: Date.now() };
91:     return providers;
92:   }
93: 
94:   return {
95:     async resolve(request?: AssistantBindingRequest): Promise<AssistantExecutionBinding> {
96:       const providerId = request?.providerId?.trim();
97:       const modelId = request?.modelId?.trim();
98: 
99:       // No explicit request → the configured default binding governs.
100:       if (!providerId || !modelId) {
101:         if (fallback) return fallback;
102:         throw new AssistantBindingError(
103:           'provider-not-found',
104:           'No provider/model was requested and no default Assistant binding is configured',
105:         );
106:       }
107: 
108:       const providers = await discover();
109:       const provider = providers.find((candidate) => candidate.id === providerId);
110:       if (!provider) {
111:         throw new AssistantBindingError('provider-not-found', `Provider not found: ${providerId}`, { providerId });
112:       }
113:       const known = provider.models?.includes(modelId);
114:       if (!known) {
115:         throw new AssistantBindingError('model-not-found', `Model not found for provider ${providerId}: ${modelId}`, {
116:           providerId,
117:           modelId,
118:         });
119:       }
120:       return { providerID: provider.id, modelID: modelId };
121:     },
122:   };
123: }

1: /**
2:  * Activity Room organizational bridge (post-ORB observability substrate).
3:  *
4:  * Feeds the organization's actual events — workflow lifecycle, acceptance
5:  * boundary, and harness stage turns — into the Activity Room's durable
6:  * projection as structured `ActivitySourceEvent`s. The room therefore renders
7:  * what the organization is doing, believing, and questioning, rather than only
8:  * the Director's messages.
9:  *
10:  * Machine-consumed organizational state comes from structured events emitted
11:  * by the organization, not from prose parsed into statuses.
12:  */
13: 
14: import type { ActivitySourceEvent } from '@vestara/activity-room';
15: import type { ActivityRoom } from '../activity-room';
16: import { getActivityRoom } from '../activity-room';
17: import type { SessionStreamAccumulator } from '../session-stream';
18: 
19: export interface ActivityRoomOrganizationalBridgeOptions {
20:   readonly eventBus: {
21:     subscribe(pattern: string, handler: (evt: ActivityRoomBridgeEvent) => void | Promise<void>): () => void;
22:   };
23:   readonly threadStore: {
24:     getThread(id: string): { metadata?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> } | undefined;
25:   };
26:   /** Injectable for tests; defaults to the process-lifetime room. */
27:   readonly room?: ActivityRoom;
28:   /** Coalesces live session narrative; injected by the API boot. */
29:   readonly streams?: SessionStreamAccumulator;
30: }
31: 
32: export interface ActivityRoomBridgeEvent {
33:   readonly id: string;
34:   readonly type: string;
35:   readonly timestamp: string;
36:   readonly actor?: { id: string; role?: string };
37:   readonly payload: Record<string, unknown>;
38: }
39: 
40: /** Organizational events that carry a workflowId in their payload. */
41: const ORGANIZATIONAL_EVENT_TYPES = new Set(['workflow.started', 'workflow.completed', 'acceptance.boundary']);
42: 
43: /** Harness stage-turn events projected as agent activity. */
44: const HARNESS_EVENT_TYPES = new Set([
45:   'harness.turn.started',
46:   'harness.outcome.completed',
47:   'harness.outcome.failed',
48:   'harness.model.completed',
49: ]);
50: 
51: /** Live runtime execution activity correlated to a participant/thread. */
52: const EXECUTION_ACTIVITY_TYPE = 'opencode.execution.activity';
53: 
54: /** Maps a normalized Vestara execution event type to a harness activity type. */
55: function executionActivityToSourceType(type: string): string | undefined {
56:   switch (type) {
57:     case 'tool.started':
58:       return 'harness.tool.started';
59:     case 'tool.completed':
60:       return 'harness.tool.completed';
61:     case 'agent.progress':
62:       return 'harness.model-response';
63:     default:
64:       return undefined; // activity/heartbeat and terminal events are not projected here
65:   }
66: }
67: 
68: export function startActivityRoomOrganizationalBridge(options: ActivityRoomOrganizationalBridgeOptions): () => void {
69:   return options.eventBus.subscribe('*', async (evt) => {
70:     try {
71:       // Resolve lazily per event: the durable room is initialized after the
72:       // bridge is wired at boot, and routes/bridge must share the same instance.
73:       const room = options.room ?? getActivityRoom();
74:       for (const event of projectSourceEvents(evt, options)) {
75:         if (event) await room.service.project(event);
76:       }
77:     } catch {
78:       // Projection persistence must never break the organizational run.
79:     }
80:   });
81: }
82: 
83: function projectSourceEvents(
84:   evt: ActivityRoomBridgeEvent,
85:   options: ActivityRoomOrganizationalBridgeOptions,
86: ): readonly ActivitySourceEvent[] {
87:   const type = evt.type;
88:   if (ORGANIZATIONAL_EVENT_TYPES.has(type)) {
89:     return [
90:       {
91:         id: evt.id,
92:         type,
93:         at: evt.timestamp,
94:         actorId: 'multi-agent-workflow',
95:         authority: 'system',
96:         workflowId: String(evt.payload.workflowId ?? ''),
97:         correlationId: undefined,
98:         payload: evt.payload,
99:       },
100:     ];
101:   }
102:   if (HARNESS_EVENT_TYPES.has(type)) {
103:     const threadId = typeof evt.payload.threadId === 'string' ? evt.payload.threadId : undefined;
104:     const thread = threadId ? options.threadStore.getThread(threadId) : undefined;
105:     const workflowId = thread?.metadata?.workflowId;
106:     return [
107:       {
108:         id: evt.id,
109:         type,
110:         at: evt.timestamp,
111:         actorId: evt.actor?.id ?? 'agent-harness',
112:         authority: 'agent',
113:         workflowId: typeof workflowId === 'string' ? workflowId : undefined,
114:         threadId,
115:         turnId: typeof evt.payload.turnId === 'string' ? evt.payload.turnId : undefined,
116:         correlationId: typeof evt.payload.correlationId === 'string' ? evt.payload.correlationId : undefined,
117:         payload: evt.payload,
118:       },
119:     ];
120:   }
121:   if (type === EXECUTION_ACTIVITY_TYPE) {
122:     const innerType = typeof evt.payload.type === 'string' ? evt.payload.type : '';
123:     const threadId = typeof evt.payload.threadId === 'string' ? evt.payload.threadId : undefined;
124:     const thread = threadId ? options.threadStore.getThread(threadId) : undefined;
125:     const workflowId = thread?.metadata?.workflowId;
126:     const activity = typeof evt.payload.activity === 'string' ? evt.payload.activity : undefined;
127:     const at = typeof evt.payload.at === 'string' ? evt.payload.at : evt.timestamp;
128: 
129:     if (innerType === 'agent.progress') {
130:       // Streamed narrative: coalesce into the participant's live stream item.
131:       // Never a per-character durable record.
132:       if (options.streams && threadId) {
133:         options.streams.update(
134:           {
135:             sessionId: typeof evt.payload.sessionId === 'string' ? evt.payload.sessionId : '',
136:             threadId,
137:             role: String(thread?.metadata?.role ?? 'developer'),
138:             agentId: String(thread?.metadata?.agentId ?? evt.actor?.id ?? 'agent'),
139:             at,
140:           },
141:           activity ?? '',
142:         );
143:       }
144:       return [];
145:     }
146: 
147:     // Semantic boundaries finalize the live narrative as ONE readable record,
148:     // and the semantic event (tool, completion) is projected distinctly.
149:     const finalized = options.streams && threadId ? options.streams.finalize(threadId, at) : undefined;
150:     const records: ActivitySourceEvent[] = [];
151:     if (finalized && finalized.text.trim().length > 0) {
152:       records.push({
153:         id: `${evt.id}-narrative`,
154:         type: 'harness.agent-message',
155:         at,
156:         actorId: evt.actor?.id ?? 'agent-harness',
157:         authority: 'agent',
158:         workflowId: typeof workflowId === 'string' ? workflowId : undefined,
159:         threadId,
160:         turnId: typeof evt.payload.turnId === 'string' ? evt.payload.turnId : undefined,
161:         correlationId: typeof evt.payload.correlationId === 'string' ? evt.payload.correlationId : undefined,
162:         payload: { threadId, content: finalized.text.trim() },
163:       });
164:     }
165: 
166:     const sourceType = executionActivityToSourceType(innerType);
167:     if (sourceType && threadId) {
168:       records.push({
169:         id: evt.id,
170:         type: sourceType,
171:         at,
172:         actorId: evt.actor?.id ?? 'agent-harness',
173:         authority: 'agent',
174:         workflowId: typeof workflowId === 'string' ? workflowId : undefined,
175:         threadId,
176:         turnId: typeof evt.payload.turnId === 'string' ? evt.payload.turnId : undefined,
177:         correlationId: typeof evt.payload.correlationId === 'string' ? evt.payload.correlationId : undefined,
178:         payload: { ...evt.payload, toolName: innerType.startsWith('tool.') ? activity : undefined },
179:       });
180:     }
181:     return records;
182:   }
183:   return [];
184: }

1: /**
2:  * ARX-015 M9: Activity Event Adapter
3:  *
4:  * Converts authoritative platform events (M8 WorkflowEvents, human messages,
5:  * agent lifecycle) into canonical ActivityEvents for durable storage.
6:  *
7:  * This adapter normalizes events to Vestara concepts. It never leaks
8:  * OpenCode internals or provider-specific response formats.
9:  */
10: 
11: import type {
12:   ActivityActor,
13:   BindingId,
14:   ExecutionId,
15:   RepositoryBindingId,
16:   RuntimeSessionId,
17:   TraceId,
18:   WorkflowEvent,
19:   WorkflowRunId,
20:   WorkflowTaskId,
21: } from '@vestara/types';
22: import type { ActivityEvent, ActivityPayload, ActivityType } from './m9-types';
23: 
24: // ─── M8 WorkflowEvent → ActivityEvent ──────────────────────
25: 
26: /** Adapter ID counter for unique event IDs. */
27: let adapterEventCounter = 0;
28: 
29: /**
30:  * Convert an M8 WorkflowEvent into a durable ActivityEvent.
31:  * The ActivityEvent carries all M1/M2 lineage from the WorkflowEvent.
32:  */
33: export function fromWorkflowEvent(event: WorkflowEvent): ActivityEvent {
34:   const eventType = mapWorkflowEventType(event.type);
35: 
36:   const payload: ActivityPayload = {
37:     message: buildWorkflowMessage(event),
38:     ...(event.output !== undefined ? { output: event.output } : {}),
39:     ...(event.error !== undefined ? { error: { message: event.error } } : {}),
40:   };
41: 
42:   return {
43:     eventId: `we-${event.workflowRunId}-${event.type}-${event.timestamp}-${++adapterEventCounter}`,
44:     type: eventType,
45:     timestamp: event.timestamp,
46:     executionId: event.executionId,
47:     traceId: event.traceId,
48:     requestId: event.requestId,
49:     workflowRunId: event.workflowRunId,
50:     taskId: event.taskInstanceId,
51:     agentAssignmentId: event.agentAssignmentId,
52:     actor: mapWorkflowActor(event),
53:     source: 'workflow-engine',
54:     payload,
55:   };
56: }
57: 
58: /**
59:  * Map M8 WorkflowEventType to canonical ActivityType.
60:  * 1:1 mapping — no normalization loss.
61:  */
62: function mapWorkflowEventType(type: WorkflowEvent['type']): ActivityType {
63:   // The WorkflowEvent types already match ActivityType 1:1
64:   return type as ActivityType;
65: }
66: 
67: /**
68:  * Determine actor from WorkflowEvent.
69:  * Workflow events are system-originated.
70:  */
71: function mapWorkflowActor(event: WorkflowEvent): ActivityActor {
72:   if (event.agentAssignmentId) {
73:     return { type: 'agent', id: event.agentAssignmentId, displayName: event.agentAssignmentId };
74:   }
75:   return { type: 'system', id: 'workflow-engine', displayName: 'Workflow Engine' };
76: }
77: 
78: /**
79:  * Build human-readable message from WorkflowEvent.
80:  * Normalized to Vestara concepts — no OpenCode leakage.
81:  */
82: function buildWorkflowMessage(event: WorkflowEvent): string {
83:   switch (event.type) {
84:     case 'workflow.started':
85:       return 'Workflow started';
86:     case 'workflow.completed':
87:       return 'Workflow completed';
88:     case 'workflow.failed':
89:       return `Workflow failed${event.error ? `: ${event.error}` : ''}`;
90:     case 'workflow.cancelled':
91:       return 'Workflow cancelled';
92:     case 'task.runnable':
93:       return `Task "${event.taskId}" is runnable`;
94:     case 'task.started':
95:       return `Task "${event.taskId}" started by agent ${event.agentAssignmentId ?? 'unknown'}`;
96:     case 'task.completed':
97:       return `Task "${event.taskId}" completed`;
98:     case 'task.failed':
99:       return `Task "${event.taskId}" failed${event.error ? `: ${event.error}` : ''}`;
100:     case 'task.cancelled':
101:       return `Task "${event.taskId}" cancelled`;
102:     default:
103:       return `Workflow event: ${event.type}`;
104:   }
105: }

107: // ─── Human Message → ActivityEvent ─────────────────────────
108: 
109: export interface HumanMessageInput {
110:   /** Message content. */
111:   readonly message: string;
112: 
113:   /** User identity. */
114:   readonly userId: string;
115: 
116:   /** Display name. */
117:   readonly displayName: string;
118: 
119:   /**
120:    * Stable message identity from the authoritative conversation service.
121:    * When provided, used to derive a deterministic eventId for deduplication.
122:    */
123:   readonly messageId?: string;
124: 
125:   /** Conversation identity. */
126:   readonly conversationId?: string;
127: 
128:   /** Workflow run context. */
129:   readonly workflowRunId?: WorkflowRunId;
130: 
131:   /** Execution context. */
132:   readonly executionId?: ExecutionId;
133: 
134:   /** Trace context. */
135:   readonly traceId?: TraceId;
136: 
137:   /** Task context. */
138:   readonly taskId?: WorkflowTaskId;
139: 
140:   /** Repository context. */
141:   readonly repositoryBindingId?: RepositoryBindingId;
142: 
143:   /** Runtime session context. */
144:   readonly runtimeSessionBindingId?: RuntimeSessionId;
145: 
146:   /** AI binding context. */
147:   readonly aiBindingId?: BindingId;
148: }
149: 
150: /**
151:  * Convert a human message into a durable ActivityEvent.
152:  * Human messages are first-class durable facts that survive restart/reconnect.
153:  *
154:  * When `messageId` is provided (from the authoritative conversation service),
155:  * the eventId is derived from it for stable deduplication across replays.
156:  * Otherwise falls back to a timestamp-based id.
157:  */
158: export function fromHumanMessage(input: HumanMessageInput): ActivityEvent {
159:   const now = new Date().toISOString();
160: 
161:   // Stable eventId: derive from authoritative messageId when available.
162:   // This ensures the same logical message produces the same M9 eventId
163:   // across normal and recovery publication (F2 deduplication).
164:   const eventId = input.messageId
165:     ? `human.message:${input.messageId}`
166:     : `hm-${input.userId}-${now}-${++adapterEventCounter}`;
167: 
168:   return {
169:     eventId,
170:     type: 'human.message',
171:     timestamp: now,
172:     executionId: input.executionId,
173:     traceId: input.traceId,
174:     workflowRunId: input.workflowRunId,
175:     taskId: input.taskId,
176:     repositoryBindingId: input.repositoryBindingId,
177:     runtimeSessionBindingId: input.runtimeSessionBindingId,
178:     aiBindingId: input.aiBindingId,
179:     actor: {
180:       type: 'human',

182:       displayName: input.displayName,
183:     },
184:     source: 'human-input',

188:       ...(input.messageId ? { messageId: input.messageId } : {}),

/**
 * Canonical execution lifecycle.
 *
 * CORE-001 found five overlapping state machines:
 *   1. ServiceStatus (9 states) — service lifecycle
 *   2. RuntimeState (11 states) — runtime lifecycle
 *   3. RuntimeSessionLifecycle (5 states) — session binding
 *   4. VestaraExecutionState (9 states) — execution-level (closest to canonical)
 *   5. ProviderStatus (6 states) — provider health
 *
 * This module establishes the canonical execution lifecycle.
 * It is distinct from runtime lifecycle, session lifecycle, and service lifecycle.
 *
 * Design rationale:
 *   - 'requested'  : Execution has been requested but not yet bound to a runtime
 *   - 'binding'    : Runtime binding in progress (provider/model resolution)
 *   - 'ready'      : Bound to runtime, waiting to start
 *   - 'running'    : Actively executing in the runtime
 *   - 'completed'  : Successfully finished (execution succeeded; verification separate)
 *   - 'failed'     : Execution failed with error
 *   - 'cancelled'  : Cancelled by user or system
 *   - 'timed_out'  : Exceeded time limit
 *
 * Terminal states: completed, failed, cancelled, timed_out
 * Non-terminal states: requested, binding, ready, running
 *
 * Valid transitions:
 *   requested → binding → ready → running → completed
 *                                             ├── failed
 *                                             ├── cancelled
 *                                             └── timed_out
 *   requested → failed (binding error)
 *   requested → cancelled (user abort before binding)
 *   binding → failed (resolution error)
 *   ready → cancelled (user abort before execution)
 *   running → failed (runtime error)
 *   running → cancelled (user abort during execution)
 *   running → timed_out (timeout exceeded)
 */

/**
 * Execution lifecycle status.
 *
 * This is the Vestara-owned execution state machine.
 * Runtime-native states must map into these values.
 */
export type ExecutionStatus =
  | 'requested'
  | 'binding'
  | 'ready'
  | 'running'
  | 'completed'
  | 'failed'
  | 'cancelled'
  | 'timed_out';

/** Terminal execution states — no further transitions possible. */
export const EXECUTION_TERMINAL_STATES: readonly ExecutionStatus[] = [
  'completed',
  'failed',
  'cancelled',
  'timed_out',
] as const;

/** Non-terminal execution states — transitions still possible. */
export const EXECUTION_NON_TERMINAL_STATES: readonly ExecutionStatus[] = [
  'requested',
  'binding',
  'ready',
  'running',
] as const;

/** Runtime type guard for terminal states. */
export function isExecutionTerminal(status: ExecutionStatus): boolean {
  return (EXECUTION_TERMINAL_STATES as readonly string[]).includes(status);
}

/**
 * Valid state transitions.
 * Key = source state, Value = set of allowed target states.
 */
export const EXECUTION_TRANSITIONS: Readonly<Record<ExecutionStatus, readonly ExecutionStatus[]>> = {
  requested: ['binding', 'failed', 'cancelled'],
  binding: ['ready', 'failed'],
  ready: ['running', 'cancelled'],
  running: ['completed', 'failed', 'cancelled', 'timed_out'],
  completed: [],
  failed: [],
  cancelled: [],
  timed_out: [],
};

/**
 * Check whether a state transition is valid.
 */
export function isValidTransition(from: ExecutionStatus, to: ExecutionStatus): boolean {
  return (EXECUTION_TRANSITIONS[from] as readonly string[]).includes(to);
}

/**
 * Activity-level execution state (distinct from lifecycle).
 *
 * While ExecutionStatus tracks the lifecycle, ExecutionActivityState
 * describes what the execution is currently doing. Tool calls are
 * activities, not lifecycle states.
 */
export type ExecutionActivityState =
  | 'idle' // No activity (between turns)
  | 'reasoning' // Model is generating text
  | 'tool_call' // Tool execution in progress
  | 'waiting' // Waiting for user input (permission/question)
  | 'enriching'; // Post-execution enrichment (diffs, todos);

26: export function queueSummary(entries: readonly QueueEntry[]): QueueSummary {
27:   const summary: QueueSummary = {
28:     total: entries.length,
29:     pending: 0,
30:     running: 0,
31:     blocked: 0,
32:     waitingApproval: 0,
33:     retrying: 0,
34:     cancelled: 0,
35:     completed: 0,
36:     failed: 0,
37:   };
38:   for (const e of entries) {
39:     const s = e.status.toLowerCase();
40:     if (s.includes('fail')) summary.failed += 1;
41:     else if (s.includes('cancel')) summary.cancelled += 1;
42:     else if (s.includes('block')) summary.blocked += 1;
43:     else if (s.includes('approv') || s === 'draft' || s === 'proposed') summary.waitingApproval += 1;
44:     else if (s.includes('retry')) summary.retrying += 1;
45:     else if (s.includes('run') || s.includes('progress') || s.includes('execut')) summary.running += 1;
46:     else if (s.includes('complete')) summary.completed += 1;
47:     else summary.pending += 1;
48:   }
49:   return summary;
50: }
51: 
52: export interface QueueSource {
53:   sessions: readonly ExecutionSessionRecord[];
54:   plans: readonly PlanRecord[];
55:   executions: readonly AgentExecutionRecord[];
56: }
57: 
58: export function buildQueue(source: QueueSource): QueueEntry[] {
59:   const out: QueueEntry[] = [];
60:   for (const s of source.sessions) {
61:     out.push({
62:       id: s.id,
63:       kind: 'session',
64:       title: s.goal || s.id,
65:       status: s.status,
66:       started: s.createdAt,
67:       updated: s.completedAt ?? s.createdAt,
68:       priority: 'normal',
69:     });
70:   }
71:   for (const p of source.plans) {
72:     out.push({
73:       id: p.id,
74:       kind: 'plan',
75:       title: p.title || p.goal || p.id,
76:       status: p.status ?? 'unknown',
77:       started: p.createdAt,
78:       updated: p.updatedAt ?? p.createdAt,
79:       priority: 'normal',
80:     });
81:     for (const t of p.tasks ?? []) {
82:       out.push({
83:         id: `${p.id}:${t.id}`,
84:         kind: 'task',
85:         title: t.summary || t.id,
86:         status: t.status ?? 'unknown',
87:         started: p.createdAt,
88:         updated: p.updatedAt ?? p.createdAt,
89:         priority: t.effort,
90:       });
91:     }
92:   }
93:   for (const e of source.executions) {
94:     out.push({
95:       id: e.id,
96:       kind: 'execution',
97:       title: e.task || e.id,
98:       status: e.status ?? 'unknown',
99:       agentId: e.agentId,
100:       started: e.startedAt,
101:       updated: e.completedAt ?? e.startedAt,
102:       priority: 'normal',
103:     });
104:   }
105:   out.sort((a, b) => (a.updated && b.updated ? (a.updated < b.updated ? 1 : -1) : 0));
106:   return out;

122: }

126:     .length;

133: ): ExecutionMetrics {
134:   const sessions = source.sessions;
135:   const executions = source.executions;
136:   const plans = source.plans;
137: 
138:   const sessionDone = sessions.filter((s) => s.status === 'completed' || s.status === 'failed');
139:   const sessionSuccess = sessionDone.filter((s) => s.status === 'completed').length;
140:   const sessionDurations = sessions
141:     .map((s) => {
142:       if (!s.createdAt || !s.completedAt) return Number.NaN;
143:       const start = new Date(s.createdAt).getTime();
144:       const end = new Date(s.completedAt).getTime();
145:       return end - start;
146:     })
147:     .filter((d) => Number.isFinite(d) && d > 0);
148: 
149:   const execDone = executions.filter((e) => e.status === 'completed' || e.status === 'failed');
150:   const execSuccess = execDone.filter((e) => e.status === 'completed').length;
151:   const execDurations = executions
152:     .map((e) => {
153:       const start = new Date(e.startedAt ?? '').getTime();
154:       const end = e.completedAt ? new Date(e.completedAt).getTime() : Date.now();
155:       return end - start;
156:     })
157:     .filter((d) => Number.isFinite(d));
158: 
159:   const taskStates = plans.flatMap((p) => (p.tasks ?? []).map((t) => t.status ?? ''));

1: /**
2:  * Orchestration event bridge — projects workflow-orchestrator events into the
3:  * temporal engineering event store as `orchestration.*` records.
4:  *
5:  * The orchestrator is a pure domain package; this bridge is the composition-
6:  * root adapter that makes its audit stream replayable alongside the existing
7:  * `harness.*` and `change.*` projections (ADR-121). Every event carries the
8:  * project as `correlationId` and task/plan ids in the payload. When an event
9:  * bus is provided, each event is also re-emitted as `orchestration.*` so the
10:  * Workspace UI surfaces them as toasts and notifications in real time.
11:  */
12: 
13: import type { SqliteEngineeringEventStore } from '@vestara/engineering-event-store';
14: import type { EventBus } from '@vestara/event-bus';
15: import type { OrchestrationEvent, OrchestrationEventSink } from '@vestara/workflow-orchestrator';
16: 
17: export interface OrchestrationEventBridgeOptions {
18:   readonly events: SqliteEngineeringEventStore;
19:   readonly workspaceId: string;
20:   readonly environmentId?: string;
21:   readonly eventBus?: EventBus;
22: }
23: 
24: type FlatOrchestrationEvent = {
25:   readonly type: string;
26:   readonly taskId?: string;
27:   readonly planId?: string;
28:   readonly projectId?: string;
29: };
30: 
31: function flat(event: OrchestrationEvent): FlatOrchestrationEvent {
32:   return event as unknown as FlatOrchestrationEvent;
33: }
34: 
35: function eventTaskId(event: OrchestrationEvent): string | undefined {
36:   const e = flat(event);
37:   return e.type.startsWith('task.') || e.type.startsWith('file.lock.') ? e.taskId : undefined;
38: }
39: 
40: function eventPlanId(event: OrchestrationEvent): string | undefined {
41:   const e = flat(event);
42:   return e.type.startsWith('plan.') ||
43:     e.type.startsWith('task.') ||
44:     e.type === 'architecture.reviewed' ||
45:     e.type === 'verification.passed' ||
46:     e.type === 'verification.failed'
47:     ? e.planId
48:     : undefined;
49: }
50: 
51: export class OrchestrationEventBridge implements OrchestrationEventSink {
52:   private readonly events: SqliteEngineeringEventStore;
53:   private readonly workspaceId: string;
54:   private readonly environmentId?: string;
55:   private readonly eventBus?: EventBus;
56: 
57:   constructor(options: OrchestrationEventBridgeOptions) {
58:     this.events = options.events;
59:     this.workspaceId = options.workspaceId;
60:     this.environmentId = options.environmentId;
61:     this.eventBus = options.eventBus;
62:   }
63: 
64:   async append(event: OrchestrationEvent): Promise<void> {
65:     const type = `orchestration.${event.type}`;
66:     await this.events.append({
67:       type,
68:       source: 'workflow-orchestrator',
69:       actorId: 'orchestrator',
70:       authority: 'system',
71:       workspaceId: this.workspaceId,
72:       environmentId: this.environmentId,
73:       taskId: eventTaskId(event),
74:       correlationId: String(event.projectId),
75:       payload: { ...(event as unknown as Record<string, unknown>), planId: eventPlanId(event) },
76:     });
77:     if (this.eventBus) {
78:       await this.eventBus
79:         .emit({
80:           type,
81:           source: 'workflow-orchestrator',
82:           actor: { id: 'orchestrator', role: 'system' },
83:           payload: { message: defaultMessage(type), ...(event as unknown as Record<string, unknown>) },
84:         })
85:         .catch(() => {});
86:     }
87:   }
88: }
89: 
90: function defaultMessage(type: string): string {
91:   switch (type) {
92:     case 'orchestration.project.completed':
93:       return 'Project completed';
94:     case 'orchestration.parent.created':
95:       return 'Multi-repo project created';
96:     case 'orchestration.parent.completed':
97:       return 'Multi-repo project completed';
98:     case 'orchestration.task.failed':
99:       return 'Task failed';
100:     case 'orchestration.task.blocked':
101:       return 'Task blocked';
102:     case 'orchestration.task.approval-requested':
103:       return 'Approval required';
104:     case 'orchestration.task.review.decided':
105:       return 'Task reviewed';
106:     case 'orchestration.task.tests.decided':
107:       return 'Tests completed';
108:     case 'orchestration.verification.failed':
109:       return 'Verification failed';
110:     case 'orchestration.plan.generated':
111:       return 'Plan generated';
112:     default:
113:       return type.replace('orchestration.', '');
114:   }
115: }

/**
 * M11C Activity Room Page
 *
 * Production Activity Room UI Shell + Live Read Surface.
 * Consumes frozen M11A HTTP read API and M11B WebSocket protocol.
 *
 * Authority flow: M9 durable truth → M10 projection → M11A/M11B → this page → UI
 *
 * No alternative Activity Room state source, polling loop, mock participant
 * system, or UI-owned workflow state is introduced.
 *
 * Acceptance criteria:
 * 1. Renders entirely from M11A/M11B production contracts
 * 2. Zero hardcoded participants
 * 3. Snapshot → catch-up → live produces no visible duplication
 * 4. Disconnect/reconnect requires no reload
 * 5. resync-required performs controlled resynchronization
 * 6. Historical pages load independently from M10's 500-item working set
 * 7. Older-history prepend preserves viewport position
 * 8. Incoming activity does not steal scroll position when reading history
